cross_cutting_intrinsic_capabilities.name: Continuous Upstream-Change Intelligence & Audit
cross_cutting_intrinsic_capabilities.purpose: Detect and assess upstream improvements, security advisories, breaking changes, deprecations, API/schema/protocol changes, CI changes and support lifecycle changes that may affect declared dependencies or planned technology choices.
cross_cutting_intrinsic_capabilities.execution: Scheduled through the existing weekly capability-discovery automation; not a repository-native CI workflow.
outputs: actual dependency inventory with exact versions and dependency paths
security advisories, breaking changes, deprecations and support/licence changes
risk-ranked recommendations with authoritative evidence links
baseline comparison and explicit evidence gaps
acceptance_criteria: Inventory actual dependencies from repository manifests and lockfiles rather than architecture notes.
Inspect relevant open pull-request branches as well as the default branch.
Verify findings against authoritative upstream release, advisory, deprecation and support sources.
Detect beneficial improvements and breaking/security changes.
Distinguish installed dependencies from planned-only watchlist entries.
Compare each run with a dated prior baseline.
Produce repeatable reports without modifying dependencies or production state.
Pass independent review of audit scope, evidence and output integrity.
known_gaps: Current default branch main exposes only README.md; active pull-request branches contain additional capability and engineering artefacts.
Actual dependency inventory must be assembled from the relevant working branches and manifests; no claim of installed status is made for the planned watchlist.
Weekly ChatGPT automation is configured, but the recurring audit has not yet completed its first run.

lineage_capacity.instruction: Do not invent lineage IDs, names, UMIC assignments or mappings.

governance.activation_requires: approved identity, provenance, licence and security review, contract compatibility, resource evaluation, tests, permission review and independent verification

known_gaps: The 99 lineage slot names, responsibilities and source mappings remain unresolved.
Most workstreams are open draft PRs and are not automatically integrated into PR 35.
The UCA source register contains duplicate references; canonical providers are deduplicated while source IDs are retained.
Candidate providers are not thereby installed, licence-cleared at selected commits, tested or production-ready.
Preserved source snapshots remain quarantined pending adaptation and target-side validation.
The 12-dimension register and 99 complementary capability set are proposed architecture records, not implemented runtime capabilities.
The exact historical 99-name draft was not recoverable; UEE-9FO-UCC-099 is a new, explicitly versioned reconstruction.
The 99 lineage slots remain unmapped and must not be populated from the complementary capability set.
Capability ownership, dependency mapping, implementation, tests and independent verification remain required before activation.

clarifications: CHRONOS is temporal reasoning; TEMPORAL is time-dependent operational governance.
AFI PRIME remains one canonical fusion function instantiated in nine governed UMIC contexts.
Dimensions are responsibility scopes, not additional UMICs, lineage slots, runtime processes or fusion authorities.

ninefold_complementary_capability_set.origin: New, explicitly versioned reconstruction. The exact historical 99-name draft was not recoverable; this file does not claim verbatim recovery.
integration_rules: This 99-capability register is distinct from the 99 lineage slots. Do not map capabilities onto lineage placeholders automatically.
The 99 lineage slots remain unresolved until approved canonical identities, roles, provenance and mappings exist.

Existing systems including STARWIRE, SYPHON, OMNISIGHT PRIME, CHRONOS VELOCITY PRIME, UPN and EUPN retain independent identities; this register adds complementary responsibilities rather than absorbing or renaming them.
OMNIVELOCITY PRIME and HYPERVELOCITY PRIME are cross-cutting performance capabilities, not dimensions, divisions, UMICs or fusion authorities.
STARWIRE discovers and preserves candidate sources; discovery is not approval or integration.
AFI PRIME coordinates specialists while preserving separate outcomes. It cannot grant itself permissions, approve its own high-impact actions or independently certify its results.
No capability activates by being listed. Lifecycle: Discovered → Proposed → Under Evaluation → Approved → Integrated / Rejected / Retired.
Before activation each capability needs an owner, interfaces, dependencies, threat model, resource profile, acceptance tests, evidence and independent verification.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly nine divisions, each with eleven unique capability records.
Each capability has a stable ID, responsibility, lifecycle and activation status.
No additional UMIC, lineage slot or fusion authority is created.
Cross-capability dependencies, overlap, conflicts and resource costs are evaluated before implementation.
Implementation and verification claims are tied to repository evidence and passing tests.
